reviews.review:
So I was looking through my list of owned games and realized I don't have anything with a hero or main protagonist as incredibly badass as Captain Titus from [b]Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine[/b]. I then made a ranking: second place is tied between Batman and Strider Hiryu while fourth place goes to the Boss from [b]Saints Row the Third[/b] who narrowly edges out The Overlord for possessing better minions. This list isn't up for debate nor is it the topic of this review, though. The topic is how playing such an overpowering character can be an experience in itself.
 
You are for all intent and purposes a giant superhuman walking tank whose main weapons are a fully automatic mini-rocket launcher and a chainsaw sword. You fly around on a rocket pack coming down with a hammer that produces an explosion of concussive force. You heal yourself in the blood and guts of your broken opponents. You can literally run through some of your lesser enemies. None of this makes the game a cakewalk: orks will mob you relentlessly with their oversized choppers, chaos forces have access to plasma cannons and there are always monsters greater in size than you. It doesn't matter. Being such a superhuman badass just pushes you to greater acts of heroism.
 
The gameplay is basic but enjoyable enough: fire those bolt shells, melee the shooters, dodge roll a lot, throw a grenade into that mess of orks, use the Rage gauge before you die... The difference is that being in control of Captain Titus makes all of this [i]so satisfying.[/i] There is weight in your run. The ground thumps as you do your dodge roll. Your bolter feels like the mini-rocket launcher it's supposed to be and not some standard machine gun. The execution scenes are barbaric, gruesome and as bloody as any [b]Mortal Kombat[/b] Fatality. It [i]enhances[/i] the gameplay, giving every one of your actions greater impact.
 
At this point, I should state that no knowledge of the Warhammer 40K lore is required to get into [b]Space Marine[/b]. What more, if by some strange circumstance you're a Warhammer enthusiast or a lapsed fan who has not yet bought the game, I can honestly say that THQ have written an Ultramarine Captain better than the current in-house team of writers. Again: the story is basic enough in a "save the empire" kind of manner but it's the glorious yet still humble Captain Titus who draws you in.
 
This is actually the main shortcoming of this game. Outside of the main story you have Multiplayer Mode WHERE YOU DO NOT control Captain Titus, playing instead as a bog standard space marine. Instead of orks you face other space marines where you'll find yourself dying in seconds to lascannons, meltaguns and insta-kill thunder hammers; often with no knowledge over how you could've prevented your death. Unlike story mode, you die A LOT and obtaining perks that would increase the effectiveness of your weapons is a frustrating experience. You will lag, you will get stuck in walls and you won't want to play again.
 
Exterminatus is an improvement and basically Co-op mode where you take on wave after wave of orks along with your friends. It's fun in a mindless slaughter sort of way but it's also a shame how the important perks needed to improve your space marine's weaponry cannot be unlocked here. It's the random challenges you'll hate the most, however. Imagine a spontaneous message tasking you to execute five headshots during a lull in the fighting where no orks are present. It just goes to show how far good but limited gameplay can go in keeping a player interested in his carnage when you'd rather play Titus with all his added abilities than chance a game with overall the same controls in a casual pick-up game of Multiplayer.

Overall; the gameplay and the controls are enjoyable enough, Captain Titus pushes all this over the top and the Multiplayer isn't worth it. Therefore, I recommend that you buy the game whenever it is at half price and ignore all of the DLC. Half price for half a product. A Thumbs Up at over 50%.
This game didn't recieve the greatest rating in the world, but it's basically like someone took Gears of War, and slapped a Warhammer 40k skin on it.
Great game - if a little short.  The game could have been so much more with co-op story mode, but it's still a fun hack-and-slash shooter.
